plan_summary:
Give the terminal failure-reason vocabulary an explicit severity split, entirely inside the two allowed paths (adws-pipeline/references/ and adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js).

Grounding observed in the worktree: (a) references/phase-gates.md documents the vocabulary as two PROSE bullet lists ("Failure-reason classes", lines 457-471) with no per-reason table and no severity column; (b) run_manifest.failure_reason is described in references/artifact-layout.md (line 52 shape, line 63 reader note) with no enum and no severity; (c) execution-report.js already computes the severity classification in NO_RETRY_REASONS + QUARANTINE_REASONS (lines 53-61) and consumes it in decideLifecycle (lines 899-921), but publishes it NOWHERE machine-readably; (d) a probe run of the shipped CLI over a copy of the canonical upheld-dissent fixture tree (parity/execution-report-fixtures/quarantine_upheld_dissent, job-4e5f6a) returns decision=QUARANTINE exit=2 with run_manifest.failure_reason=null and report.failure_reason=null - the token ADVOCATE_DISSENT exists ONLY inside the consensus gate's free-text `detail` string. The same holds for the evidence-integrity fixtures (job-9b2e14 etc.): failure_reason=null, and the only trace of the breach is the literal prose "EVIDENCE INTEGRITY: ..." in the skills_clean gate detail. That is exactly the re-derivation-by-parsing that AC-4 forbids, and it is why an upheld dissent and an integrity breach are today indistinguishable from a retriable {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE in run_manifest.failure_reason.

The change has two halves that meet in the middle:

1. execution-report.js becomes the SOURCE of severity. Keep NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS byte-identical as the single classification (so decideLifecycle is untouched and no verdict moves), and add on top of them: a `failureReasonSeverity(reason)` helper returning 'non-retriable' | 'retriable' | null computed from those same two Sets; one NEW closed-enum member EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH added to NO_RETRY_REASONS (additive - no existing reason is redefined); a nullable `failure_reason` property on the gate objects the two non-retriable conditions produce (evalConsensus's blocking-dissent FAIL branch emits ADVOCATE_DISSENT; evalSkillsClean's two integrity FAIL branches emit EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH) so the reason is a field rather than a substring of `detail`; and two additive top-level report fields - `terminal_failure_reason` (first non-null gate reason in a documented precedence order, else run_manifest.failure_reason) and `failure_severity` (that reason's severity via the helper). Exports gain `failureReasonSeverity` and `TERMINAL_FAILURE_REASON_PRECEDENCE`.

2. references/ becomes the authoritative, severity-bearing table. phase-gates.md's prose class lists are replaced by ONE canonical table with a row per reason and a Severity column (plus an in-run 'no-retry' column, because PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED is no-retry yet classified retriable by the script - the two axes must not be conflated), immediately followed by the reason-selection precedence rule that makes ADVOCATE_DISSENT and EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH beat the {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE fallback, and by the sourcing rule (read severity from execution_report.json, never from gate detail prose). artifact-layout.md pins run_manifest.failure_reason as a closed enum owned by that table and documents the new report fields (append-only rule 8 makes an undocumented extra key schema drift, so this is required, not cosmetic). validator-inputs.md's execution-report.js rows carry the same sourcing rule where an orchestrator actually looks up the script.

Deliberate boundaries. No new reference FILE: scripts/local-ci/frontmatter-lint.mjs enforces a BIDIRECTIONAL index (every references/*.md must be named in SKILL.md), and SKILL.md is outside allowed_paths - so a new file would fail Tier-1 CI with no in-scope fix. SCHEMA_VERSION stays '1.4.0': parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js line 444 asserts it exactly and parity/ is a blocked path, so a bump the file's own additive-change convention would suggest cannot be paired with its fixture update in this job; the builder records that deferral as a comment beside SCHEMA_VERSION where a reviewer reads it. No routing change for any existing reason (constraint 2), no new gate key, no decision/exit-code vocabulary change (non-goal 1), no fixture edits - the corpus keeps scoring the same decision and exit code because no fixture records either affected token in run_manifest and the new fields are additive keys the runner never compares.

Out-of-scope consequence the operator must decide on (NOT planned, because the file is outside allowed_paths): adws-pipeline/skill-manifest.json is a content digest of every shipped file under adws-pipeline/, and scripts/local-ci/skill-manifest.mjs fails the Tier-1 gate when it is stale. Editing four shipped files without regenerating it makes `make local-ci` red on the skill-manifest step alone. See phase_log.md.

file_change_proposal.description: Publish the severity classification the script already computes, and add the one missing non-retriable reason. (1) Add 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH' to NO_RETRY_REASONS (lines 53-59) - purely additive, so decideLifecycle's existing branches route it to QUARANTINE with the 'evidence preserved for review' wording and no existing reason changes meaning. (2) Add `failureReasonSeverity(reason)` returning 'non-retriable' when NO_RETRY_REASONS or QUARANTINE_REASONS contains the reason, 'retriable' for any other non-empty string, null for null/absent - computed FROM the same two Sets decideLifecycle reads, so there is one classification and it cannot drift from the verdict. (3) Give the gate objects that represent a non-retriable condition a nullable `failure_reason` property: evalConsensus's blocking-dissent FAIL branch -> 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT' (covers unresolved AND operator-upheld, which the gate already distinguishes), evalSkillsClean's unreadable-evidence branch (line 745) and mismatch branch (line 765) -> 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH'; every other gate keeps it null. This is what turns the reason from a substring of `detail` into a field. (4) In buildReport's gates.map (lines 1387-1391) emit `failure_reason: g.failure_reason || null` alongside gate/result/detail, and add two top-level fields to the report object: `terminal_failure_reason` = the first non-null gate failure_reason scanned in a frozen, exported precedence order (integrity before dissent before the rest, matching the existing SC-8/F-55 comment at line 982 that an integrity breach outranks the verdict it was hiding), falling back to run_manifest's failureReason; and `failure_severity` = failureReasonSeverity(terminal_failure_reason). (5) Render both in renderMarkdown near line 1103 so the .md reader sees the severity too. (6) Export failureReasonSeverity and the precedence constant. (7) Leave SCHEMA_VERSION at '1.4.0' with a comment stating why the additive-change bump is deferred (parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js pins 1.4.0 and parity/ is a blocked path for this contract). Do not touch decideLifecycle, exitCodeFor, DECISIONS, GATE_STATUSES, or any gate key.

Turn the 'Failure-reason classes' section (lines 457-471) from two prose bullet lists into the canonical severity-bearing TABLE plus the two rules that make it usable, and update the Contents bullet on line 11 to name it. The table carries one row per terminal reason - CREDENTIAL_FAILURE, OPERATOR_CANCEL, MISSING_UPSTREAM_ARTIFACT, PLAN_COHERENCE_BELOW_THRESHOLD (reserved), ADVOCATE_DISSENT, EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH (new), PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED, PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, and the seven concrete {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE values as one parameterized row - with columns: Reason | Severity (retriable / non-retriable, defined as exactly what execution-report.js's NO_RETRY_REASONS + QUARANTINE_REASONS classify, so AC-1's severity and AC-4's source are the same fact) | In-run retry (no-retry = terminate immediately ignoring remaining budget; this second axis is why PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED can be no-retry AND retriable, a distinction the current prose already makes and that a single column would destroy) | Verdict | When the orchestrator records it. Directly under the table add (a) the REASON-SELECTION PRECEDENCE rule: a condition named in this table always wins over the {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE fallback, so an unresolved or operator-upheld Advocate dissent records ADVOCATE_DISSENT and never REVIEW_GATE_FAILURE/TEST_GATE_FAILURE, and an evidence-integrity breach records EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH - {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE means 'budget exhausted and nothing more specific applies', nothing else; (b) the SOURCING rule: the orchestrator reads severity and the reason from execution_report.json's `failure_severity` / `terminal_failure_reason` (or the per-gate `failure_reason`), never by pattern-matching a gate `detail` string; (c) a restatement that the vocabulary is a CLOSED enum, that ADVOCATE_DISSENT_REPAIRED and CRITIC_FAIL_REPAIRED remain attempt-only annotations outside it (preserving lines 210-213 and 398-403), and that reasons may be added but never redefined. Also add one clause at the uphold bullet (lines 371-373) and at the consensus terminal-enforcement rule pointing at the table, so the resolution vocabulary and the reason vocabulary cannot drift apart again.

Make the evidence-layout contract carry the severity split, in the two places a reader looks for it. (1) At the run_manifest.json field notes (around lines 60-68, where final_status's four values are already enumerated), state that failure_reason is a CLOSED enum whose single authority is the terminal failure-reason table in references/phase-gates.md, that every value carries a severity there, that EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH is the value for an evidence-integrity termination, and that an upheld/unresolved dissent is recorded as ADVOCATE_DISSENT rather than a {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE - so the file that defines the field stops being silent about its vocabulary. (2) Document the report's new fields: append-only rule 8 (lines 463-468) declares an undocumented extra key to be schema drift, and rule 5 (lines 456-457) currently says only that execution_report.{json,md} are derived - so add a short `execution_report.json` entry to the File shapes section (and its Contents bullet on lines 7-9) naming `failure_reason` (verbatim from run_manifest), `terminal_failure_reason`, `failure_severity`, and the per-gate `gates[].failure_reason`, stating that these are the orchestrator's sourcing surface for severity and that the file remains derived and never hand-edited. Without this the four new keys would themselves be schema drift by the repo's own rule.

Put the sourcing rule where an orchestrator actually looks the script up, so AC-4 holds at the point of use rather than only in phase-gates.md. In the 'Non-validator scripts' table (line 94) extend the execution-report.js Notes cell: besides the 0/10/1/2 exit mapping it also emits `terminal_failure_reason` and `failure_severity` (retriable | non-retriable), which is where the orchestrator READS the severity of the reason it is about to record - never by parsing a gate `detail` string. Mirror one clause in the 'Verdict vocabularies and exit codes' table row for execution-report.js (line 113) so the severity field sits beside the `decision` vocabulary it complements, and keep the existing 'exit 3 = could not run' text and the surrounding 'A validator's fail is exit 0' paragraph untouched. Documentation-only: no vocabulary in this file changes.

criteria_map.criterion: The terminal failure reason vocabulary documents, for every reason, whether that reason is retriable or non-retriable, and the severity is stated in the same table the reason is defined in.
criteria_map.check_idea: Parse the 'Failure-reason classes' section of adws-pipeline/references/phase-gates.md and assert it contains a markdown table whose header has a Severity column and whose rows cover every reason token the section names; assert each row's severity cell is exactly 'retriable' or 'non-retriable' (closed values, no prose severity); assert the row set includes ADVOCATE_DISSENT, EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH, PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED, PR_DRIFT_SENTINEL_BLOCK, STABILITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED and the {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE row; and cross-check the table against the script by requiring adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js and asserting failureReasonSeverity(row.reason) === row.severity for every row - the table and the code cannot disagree. RED baseline: the section today is two prose bullet lists (`grep -c '^| ' between the section heading and the next '## '` is 0) and no severity is attached to any individual reason, so both the table assertion and the per-row cross-check fail pre-change.

criteria_map.criterion: An upheld advocate dissent terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: Copy parity/execution-report-fixtures/quarantine_upheld_dissent/artifacts/job-4e5f6a (the canonical resolution.action='uphold' tree) into the tester's scratch root - never run against the corpus in place - run `node adws-pipeline/scripts/execution-report.js <copy>` and assert on the emitted execution_report.json: gates.find(g=>g.gate==='consensus').failure_reason === 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT', terminal_failure_reason === 'ADVOCATE_DISSENT', failure_severity === 'non-retriable', and that terminal_failure_reason does NOT match /_GATE_FAILURE$/; also assert decision==='QUARANTINE' and exit code 2 are unchanged from baseline. Pair it with a docs assertion that phase-gates.md's precedence rule names the upheld/unresolved dissent as recording ADVOCATE_DISSENT and forbids {PHASE}_GATE_FAILURE for it. RED baseline: measured on this fixture pre-change - run_manifest.failure_reason is null, report.failure_reason is null, no terminal_failure_reason or failure_severity key exists, and the only occurrence of the token is inside the consensus gate's free-text detail string.

criteria_map.criterion: An evidence integrity breach terminates on a distinct non-retriable failure reason rather than on the blanket phase gate failure reason.
criteria_map.check_idea: Same shape as the dissent check, over a scratch copy of parity/execution-report-fixtures/quarantine_trace_mismatch/artifacts/job-9b2e14 (trace-vs-validator forgery) and, for the second integrity branch, quarantine_unreadable_manifest/artifacts/job-unr001 with its declared chmod: assert gates.find(g=>g.gate==='skills_clean').failure_reason === 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH', terminal_failure_reason === 'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH', failure_severity === 'non-retriable', no /_GATE_FAILURE$/ match, and decision/exit unchanged at QUARANTINE/2. Add a unit-level assertion that require('execution-report.js').NO_RETRY_REASONS.has('EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH') is true and that decideLifecycle({status:'failed', failureReason:'EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_BREACH', gates:[]}).decision === 'QUARANTINE' (a `failed` run carrying the new token must not be routed to RETRY), plus a docs assertion that the reason appears as a non-retriable row in the phase-gates table and in artifact-layout.md's failure_reason enum note. RED baseline: the token does not exist anywhere in the tree today (grep returns nothing outside this plan), both fixtures report failure_reason null, and the breach is discoverable only via the literal 'EVIDENCE INTEGRITY' prose in the skills_clean detail.

criteria_map.criterion: The severity of a terminal failure reason is sourced from the classification execution-report.js already computes, not re-derived by an orchestrator parsing gate detail strings.
criteria_map.check_idea: Three-part check. (a) Single source: require the module and assert failureReasonSeverity is exported and that for EVERY member of NO_RETRY_REASONS and QUARANTINE_REASONS it returns 'non-retriable', for a token in neither ('BUILD_GATE_FAILURE', 'PROTECTED_BRANCH_BLOCKED') 'retriable', and for null/undefined/'' null - proving severity is a projection of the sets decideLifecycle itself reads rather than a second hand-maintained list; falsify by asserting the two Sets are still exported and still contain their original members (no existing reason silently reclassified). (b) No parsing required: over scratch copies of the upheld-dissent and trace-mismatch fixtures, assert failure_severity and terminal_failure_reason are present as first-class JSON fields and that deleting every gate `detail` string from the parsed report still leaves both fields fully determined - i.e. a reader that never reads `detail` gets the same answer. (c) Docs: assert phase-gates.md and validator-inputs.md both state that severity is read from execution_report.json and never derived from gate detail prose. Guard check for the constraint: re-run `node parity/execution-report-fixtures/run-tests.js` (read-only over the corpus; its derived execution_report.{json,md} are gitignored) and require all 25 fixtures still report the same decision, warn_flag and exit code, and `git status --porcelain parity/` to be empty. RED baseline: no severity accessor is exported today (module exports are buildReport, generateExecutionReport, decideLifecycle, exitCodeFor, DECISIONS, GATE_STATUSES, PHASE_NAMES, NO_RETRY_REASONS, QUARANTINE_REASONS, SCHEMA_VERSION) and the report carries no severity field at all, so (a) and (b) fail pre-change.
